October 23, 2026


Mark Feltner
Technology Principal, Nuclear Power
Long Mott Energy, LLC
530 Gaither Road, Suite 700
Rockville, MD 20850

SUBJECT:             LONG MOTT ENERGY, LLC – SUMMARY REPORT FOR THE AUDITS
                     OF THE LONG MOTT GENERATING STATION CONSTRUCTION
                     PERMIT APPLICATION (EPID NO. L-2025-CPS-0000)

Dear Mr. Feltner:

By letter dated March 31, 2025 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System
(ADAMS) Package Accession No. ML25090A057), Long Mott Energy, LLC (LME) submitted a
construction permit (CP) application for a reactor facility pursuant to Title 10 of the Code of
Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 50, “Domestic Licensing of Production and Utilization
Facilities,” to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) for review and approval. The
facility, referred to as Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS), would be constructed in Calhoun
County, Texas. By letter dated May 12, 2025, the NRC staff (the staff) accepted the CP
application for detailed review (ML25115A247). The NRC staff conducted a detailed review of
the LMGS CP application and engaged in regulatory audits as described below to assist the
NRC staff in its review. Revision 1 of the CP application was submitted by LME on September
18, 2026.


To assist with the detailed technical review of the CP application, the NRC staff conducted
regulatory audits via LME’s electronic reading room (eRR), in-person, and through a series of
video teleconference audit discussions. The audits focused on the review of the CP application
supporting documents associated with questions identified within the audit plans
(ML25128A332, ML25156A350, ML26048A641) and additional questions identified while
reviewing the CP application. The enclosures as described below, provide details pertaining to
the activities associated with these audits. Enclosure 1 of this letter is a memorandum detailing
key aspects of the audits. Enclosure 2 (Proprietary) details the staff’s audit questions and LME’s
resolutions relating to the general audit. Enclosure 3 (Proprietary) details the staff’s audit
questions and LME’s resolutions relating to the probabilistic risk assessment audit. Enclosure 4
(Proprietary) details the staff’s audit questions and LME’s resolutions relating to the chapter 2
and structures audit. Enclosure 5 lists the documents provided by LME in the eRR for the NRC
staff to audit.

This summary report does not make any licensing conclusions or findings, but it is part of the
administrative record of the NRC staff’s review of the CP application and may provide
 M. Feltner


information supporting the NRC staff’s safety evaluation. The NRC staff exited the audits on
October 23, 2026.

If you have questions about this matter, please contact me at (301)-415-4093 or via email at
Adrian.Muniz@nrc.gov.


                                            Sincerely,



                                                           Signed by Adrian Muniz Gonzalez on
                                            10/23/26

                                            Adrian Muñiz, Senior Project Manager
                                            Advanced Reactor Licensing Branch 5
                                            Division of Advanced Reactor Licensing
                                            Office of Advanced Reactors
